title: Product and business reality
method: Describe what is available, how it is made, and what the creator can substantiate. Keep assumptions explicit.

title: Purpose and principles
method: Begin with the creator's reason for making the product. State the belief and show a decision in making or operating that it would change.

title: Character and point of view
method: Describe how the product sees the world. Express character through material, behavior, and a specific point of view.

title: Organizing idea
method: Compress the connection between the creator's belief, the product's character, and the tension that gives it meaning. It should guide a concrete design or product decision.

title: Brand boundaries
method: State what the creator will preserve and what choices would betray the idea. Identify visual, behavioral, and factual boundaries.

title: Naming and brand architecture
method: Respect existing approved names. Propose how products and extensions relate to the parent. Treat a new name as a proposal.

title: Narrative and messaging
method: Write the brand's story and an internal manifesto rooted in the creator's point of view. Show how the story can be expressed to others while preserving its meaning.

title: Verbal identity
method: Show the voice in actual sentences. Pair specific language choices with counterexamples.

title: Visual identity
method: Define logo use, roles for real colors and type, and rules someone can follow. Distinguish existing assets from design proposals.

title: Art direction and sensory identity
method: Describe subject, framing, light, texture, and motion. Give a shot or scene the team could produce. Address sound where relevant.

title: Design system
method: Show what stays consistent across layouts and what can change with the story. Give a repeatable composition rule.

title: Audience
method: Identify who can recognize and value the worldview in the approved identity. Name relevant situations and keep unverified audience assumptions explicit.

title: Market and category
method: Describe evidenced alternatives and conventions. Mark any comparison that still needs research.

title: Opportunity and positioning
method: Explain where the established identity can have meaning in the category. Name supported differences and the tradeoff without rewriting the creator's purpose.

title: Brand experience
method: Choose a customer journey moment and demonstrate how the brand behaves before, during, and after it.

title: Creative applications
method: Show the same organizing idea adapted to a few relevant formats. Write actual examples.

title: Production guidance
method: Specify inputs, references, exclusions, and review criteria a person or AI can use to produce work.

title: On-brand test
method: Ask a few short questions an editor can answer against the actual asset, promise, proof, and chosen context.

title: Governance and assets
method: Explain approved versions, approved files, contextual exceptions, and which decisions need review. Do not invent asset owners.
